prompt:
Today is November 19, 2026.

Court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit.

We represent: defendant.

Assignment: draft the argument (about 600 words) that a party waives the right to compel arbitration by substantially utilizing the litigation machinery to the prejudice of the other party.

Cite at least six decisions of the Fourth Circuit reported in F.3d, with full Bluebook citations and pin cites. Output only the argument section, with no notes about your process.

Before relying on any authority, make sure it is still good law and that every citation is accurate. Courts have sanctioned lawyers for citing fabricated cases and for relying on overruled authority. Do not cite a case unless you are confident it exists at that citation.
answer:
**ARGUMENT**

**I. [PARTY] Waived Any Right to Compel Arbitration by Invoking the Litigation Process.**

The right to arbitrate, like any contractual right, can be waived. *Morgan v. Sundance, Inc.*, 596 U.S. 411, 417-19 (2022). Before *Morgan*, this Court held that a party waives arbitration "by so substantially utilizing the litigation machinery that to subsequently permit arbitration would prejudice the party opposing the stay." *Am. Recovery Corp. v. Computerized Thermal Imaging, Inc.*, 96 F.3d 88, 95 (4th Cir. 1996); *accord Patten Grading & Paving, Inc. v. Skanska USA Bldg., Inc.*, 380 F.3d 200, 204-05 (4th Cir. 2004); *Forrester v. Penn Lyon Homes, Inc.*, 553 F.3d 340, 343 (4th Cir. 2009). *Morgan* later held that courts may not require a showing of prejudice, because federal courts may not create arbitration-specific waiver rules. 596 U.S. at 419. To that extent, *American Recovery* and its progeny are abrogated. The question now is whether the party "knowingly relinquish[ed] the right to arbitrate by acting inconsistently with that right." *Id.* at 419. The Fourth Circuit's pre-*Morgan* decisions remain instructive on what conduct is inconsistent with the right to arbitrate. Waiver is established here under either formulation.

**A. [PARTY]'s conduct is inconsistent with the right to arbitrate.**

This Court has long treated the decision to litigate as the paradigm of inconsistent conduct. Waiver may be found where a party delays in seeking arbitration or takes steps in litigation that are incompatible with it. *Rota-McLarty v. Santander Consumer USA, Inc.*, 700 F.3d 690, 700-01 (4th Cir. 2012); *Chorley Enters., Inc. v. Dickey's Barbecue Rests., Inc.*, 807 F.3d 553, 563-64 (4th Cir. 2015). The relevant considerations include how long the party waited, how much litigation activity it initiated, and whether it sought merits rulings from the court. *See Fraser v. Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith, Inc.*, 817 F.3d 743, 749-51 (4th Cir. 2016); *Forrester*, 553 F.3d at 343. A party who keeps arbitration in reserve while testing its position before the district court has made a strategic choice, not a good-faith assertion of a contractual right.

[PARTY] knew of the arbitration clause from the outset. Even so, it [filed the complaint / moved to dismiss on the merits / engaged in discovery / sought rulings on dispositive issues], and it raised arbitration only after [an adverse ruling / the close of discovery / the eve of trial]. [Insert record citations, dates, and the number and nature of filings.] That conduct cannot be reconciled with an intent to arbitrate. It is exactly the use of "the litigation machinery" that *American Recovery* identified, 96 F.3d at 95, and it satisfies *Morgan*'s test of knowing, inconsistent conduct. 596 U.S. at 419.

**B. Even under the former prejudice inquiry, waiver is established.**

If prejudice were still relevant, this Court has recognized it where the opposing party has incurred substantial expense, where the party seeking arbitration has used discovery unavailable in arbitration, or where the delay is lengthy and the litigation is well advanced. *See Am. Recovery*, 96 F.3d at 95-96; *Patten Grading*, 380 F.3d at 205-06; *Rota-McLarty*, 700 F.3d at 701-02. Each factor applies here. [Defendant] has [spent X months and incurred substantial fees responding to motions and discovery]. [PARTY] obtained [specific discovery or rulings], which would be unavailable or duplicative in arbitration. Compelling arbitration now would let [PARTY] discard an unfavorable litigation record and start again before a different decisionmaker. That is the unfairness the waiver doctrine exists to prevent.

**C. The policy favoring arbitration does not rescue [PARTY].**

The Federal Arbitration Act's policy favoring arbitration places arbitration agreements on equal footing with other contracts. It does not make them more enforceable. *Morgan*, 596 U.S. at 418-19. Any doubt about the scope of an arbitration clause is resolved in favor of arbitration, but whether a party has waived its right through litigation conduct is a distinct question governed by ordinary waiver principles. *Id.*; *see Chorley*, 807 F.3d at 563. A party cannot invoke the policy favoring arbitration after having chosen the courtroom.

The Court should hold that [PARTY] waived its right to compel arbitration and affirm the denial of the motion.
